To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
food deprivation results in a decrease in the hepistic growth hormone receptor level and in an increase in the hepatic lipid level of the fish.

food deprivation in black seabream results in a significant decrease in hepatic expression of growth hormone (GHR) receptor and a significant decrease in serum level of thyroid hormone, triiodothyronines (T(3)), with a concomitant increase in the serum level of growth hormone (T(3)).
food deprivation in black seabream resulted in a significant downregulation of hepatic GHR expression at both the mRNA and protein level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of food deprivation (starvation) on the expression of GHR, and the possible link with changes in serum hormone levels, in the liver of black seabrem.
the effects of starvation on hepatic GHR expression and serum GH and T(3) level, and hepatic proximal composition of black seabream ( Acanthopagr us schlegeli).
the regulation of growth hormone receptor in a fish species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the decrease in GHR binding and mRNA content was associated with the increased level of GH and decreased level of T(3) during starvation, and that the increase in hepatic lipid content and the decrease in the condition factor of starved fish could be related to the changes in hepatic GFR level and GH and T(3) status.
food deprivation results in an increase in the hepatic lipid level, a decrease in the hepic protein content, a decrease in serum T(3), and an increase in serum GH levels.
the liver of black seabrem A. schlegeli is responsive to food deprivation in terms of its GH receptor and proximate compositions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the decrease in hepatic GH binding and GHR mRNA content during starvation may be a consequence of the increased serum GH level, which in turn is a consequence of decreased serum T(3), and that the increased serum T(3)/GH ratio may be the cause of increased hepatic lipid content in the starved seabream.
the hepatic GHSR mRNA and protein levels are regulated in a coordinated manner in black seabream.

food deprivation in black seabream results in a marked down regulation in hepatic GFR expression, and that this down regulation may be mediated by the increased serum GH level and the decreased serum T(3).
The main takeaway from our work is that
food deprivation results in a decrease in the level of GHR in the liver of black seabrem.
the hepatic GHSR mRNA level in the black seabream A. schlegeli is not a reliable indicator of the receptor protein level.

food deprivation in black seabream leads to a significant downregulation in hepatic GFR expression at the protein and mRNA levels, with the decrease in the mRNA level less pronounced than the receptor binding level.
